data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'hector', which means 'helper'. In Greek mythology, Hector was a Trojan prince and a great warrior. In Christianity, Hector is revered as a saint and is often associated with strength and protection. The name Héctor carries the meaning “Helper” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Héctor usually hope their child will grow to embody helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Héctor is historically rooted in Greek mythology, symbolizing bravery and strength as a prominent Trojan prince and warrior. This cultural legacy has carried on to this day, with the name continuing to evoke images of valor, resolve, and leadership. Additionally, the name Héctor has spread to various Latin American countries, where it has become a common male given name.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, St. Héctor is revered as a patron saint, particularly in Spain and Portugal. As a helper and protector, this saint is believed to intercede on behalf of those in need, offering spiritual guidance, support, and solace. Thus, the name Héctor carries not only the historical significance of ancient Greek heroism but also resonates with a deeper spiritual meaning, embodying the virtues of strength, assistance, and faithfulness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Héctor, derived from the Greek name Hektor, means "holder of the heel" or "hinderer." In Christian context, it symbolizes standing firm in faith, being a protector and overcoming adversity despite setbacks.

historical_references.reference: According to the ancient Greek epic poem 'Iliad', Héctor was a Trojan prince, the son of King Priam, and the greatest warrior of the Trojans during the Trojan War. He was married to Andromache, and his son was Astyanax. Héctor was known for his courage and leadership on the battlefield, and he was revered by the Trojans as their defender and protector. However, in the final book of the Iliad, Hector is killed by Achilles, and his death marks a turning point in the war.
historical_references.time_period: The Trojan War occurred around the late 13th or early 12th century BCE.

historical_references.reference: In Christian legend, Héctor is said to have been the name of a Roman soldier who converted to Christianity and was martyred during the persecutions of Emperor Diocletian in the late 3rd century CE. According to tradition, Héctor was a centurion stationed in Gaul, and when he refused to offer sacrifice to the pagan gods, he was tortured and then beheaded. He is often depicted in art as holding the sword with which he was killed, and his shrine was a popular pilgrimage site in medieval Europe.
